determinism.canonicalization: strict duplicate-rejecting compact sorted ASCII JSON with one LF, NFC strings, no floats, bounded integers and full lowercase SHA-256
determinism.inventory: objects are sorted by full digest, semantic records follow manifest ordinal order, and missing or surplus bytes fail rather than normalize
determinism.platform: no platform, path, clock, locale, environment, process, filesystem or arrival-order input is observed
determinism.recomputation: pure session, route, planner, portfolio codec, event and logical-report rules are executed in fixed order with closed failure precedence
determinism.result: identical hostile inputs produce byte-identical replay results across fresh processes, hash seeds, Python 3.10 through 3.14, and Linux, macOS and Windows

effects.memory: bounded hostile-byte parsing, content indexing, pure upstream recomputation, event/report reconstruction, and immutable result construction
effects.mutation: inputs are not mutated and returned values own immutable byte and tuple state
effects.solver: none; producer and checker work is never rerun

ensures: The function is total over ordinary malformed, noncanonical, duplicate, missing, surplus, stale, corrupt, reordered, unsupported, truncated, and over-budget inputs and returns one closed immutable complete, invalid, or exhausted non-authoritative result.

A complete result is possible only after strict canonical parsing, exact object tuple type and sorted unique digest closure, schema and contract binding, record and content identity checks, semantic role closure, and complete manifest identity reconstruction.

Replay reconstructs the current problem-session event/artifact closure and normalized-input binding, freshly reruns pure capability routing and deterministic planning, and byte-compares the recorded route and plan without launching a producer, checker, solver, subprocess, thread, or network operation.

Replay strictly parses and cross-links the portfolio request/result, descriptors, bindings, initial/intermediate/final ledgers, attempts, transitions, validated Evidence, Certificate and checker decision bytes and rejects any selected promotion not already justified by the exact accepted checker chain.

Replay requires one exact worker-observation preimage for each visited producer and checker, recomputes its result identity, reconstructs the deterministic worker request from the accepted plan, binding, artifact closure and ledger position, and rejects any mismatch before returning complete.

Replay independently derives the only permitted event list and previous-event chain from validated lifecycle and attempt order and byte-compares it with the manifest; caller-authored event order or status fields never win.
Replay independently derives the logical report projection, validates its exact bytes and digest, and returns a stable result identity; it never repairs or emits a replacement bundle.

Raw effect inputs, machine paths, environment values, credentials, argv, clocks, PIDs, handles, unvalidated output, and arbitrary metadata are rejected if present because no accepted schema field can carry them.

A complete replay preserves the portfolio status, verdict and authority tier as recorded evidence only; the replay result always has mathematical_authority false and cannot substitute for Evidence, Certificate, or fresh mathematical checking.
MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit propagate unchanged and never become a complete replay.

Before semantic reconstruction, replay validates the manifest and every governed nested value against the exact active content-addressed schema graph, including resolved v2 object/event leaves and v3 manifest/worker roots and the v4 replay root.

Replay independently derives and byte-compares the complete semantic object role-ID sequence; changing record order and repairing ordinals, record identities, event identities, report identities, or the manifest identity remains invalid.

The empty-attempt prelaunch-invalid transcript is complete only when the recorded forensic final ledger exactly equals the initial ledger, the upstream portfolio result retains no ledger endpoints, and no worker, evidence, decision, certificate, or reconciled-ledger record exists.

epistemics.authority: replay may preserve a previously selected exact Certificate authority tier as history but cannot create, upgrade, weaken or transfer it
epistemics.checker: recorded checker bytes are strictly parsed and linked but no checker is executed during logical replay
epistemics.complete: means the recorded bundle is closed, canonical and logically reproducible under the exact accepted contracts; it is not a new proof or checker run
epistemics.exhausted: means replay input exceeded an accepted finite parser or work budget and carries no mathematical implication
epistemics.invalid: means at least one structural, identity, dependency, safe-field, event, report or authority relation failed and no partial record is trusted
epistemics.producer: never executed or trusted during replay

invariants: The object tuple contains exactly one byte string for each distinct manifest content digest including the exact logical report and no additional bytes.

Object ordinals and role IDs are contiguous/canonical and unique, content digests and lengths match, allowed alias records name identical bytes explicitly, and every required singleton role occurs exactly once.

The normalized input is the unique object named by the nested route request; current session events/artifacts, context and obligation identities are complete and no cross-session or stale-head substitution survives fresh routing.
Fresh pure routing and planning are byte-identical to their recorded objects; descriptor, binding, strategy, component, artifact and budget identities match the portfolio request and result.
Every attempt, inconclusive record, transition, selected artifact and ledger link is exact; a repaired result digest cannot hide an invalid inner chain.

Worker-observation role IDs are canonical by attempt and phase; their request, result, status, reason, strategy, artifact, Evidence, Certificate, decision and ledger links are independently derived and exact.
Event kinds, phases, outcomes, subjects, budget links, ordinals and previous digests exactly equal the independently derived sequence, with no timestamp or caller extension field.

The logical report exactly equals the independent stable projection and excludes runtime ledger events, machine details and ambient data while retaining declared budget limits and semantic classifications.
Complete, invalid and exhausted result combinations are closed; only complete carries manifest, bundle and logical report identities plus portfolio classification.
Public values are final, immutable, constructor-owned, non-pickle authority and freshly revalidated before serialization.
Any unknown field, duplicate key, float, bool-as-int, NUL, non-NFC string, excessive nesting/count/bytes, hash repair, reorder, omission, surplus or cross-run swap fails closed.

Worker result artifact inventories are empty for unvalidated output and contain exact governed stdout metadata only when linked to retained Evidence or a validated checker envelope; invalid output content digests are never accepted as semantic observation data.
Runtime replay result contract and schema constants are MH-C-RUN-AUDIT-REPLAY-004 and mathhead.run-audit-replay-result.v4 exactly.
raises: RunAuditValidationError is raised only by explicitly requested strict replay-result parsers, serializers, accessors, and validators, not for ordinary hostile bundle bytes handled by replay_run_audit.
PermissionError and TypeError protect direct construction, subclassing and pickling of public replay values.
MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit propagate unchanged.
requires: MH-C-WORKFLOW-001 governs this critical parser, replay checker, serialization, and trust boundary.
manifest is exact built-in bytes and objects is an exact built-in tuple of exact built-in bytes; every value is hostile and carries no authority by presentation.

The replay implementation binds the exact accepted MH-C-AUDITED-RUN-004 and upstream problem-session, capability-registry, deterministic-planner, proof-search-portfolio, ResourceBudget, Evidence, Certificate, TheoryPlugin, isolated-worker, and trust-transition identities from the accepted contract manifest.
